description: SASRec models next-item preference using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Candidate scores are dot products between the final sequence representation and shared item embeddings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
motivation: Attention lets the model select useful past interactions, balancing recent-item dependence in sparse histories with longer-range context in denser histories. SASRec does not itself solve zero-interaction user or unseen-item cold start; its learned item representations depend on interaction data. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781)
implementation_notes: Use the existing RecHarness sasrec_perdataset implementation as the starting point. Preserve all four category routes, fixed splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, whose supplied default is 200. Select configurations using only macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Retain the required diagnosis interfaces and measured metric definitions; unavailable reviews, ratings and simulator traits must remain unobserved. Any architecture change must update the predictor writer and compatibility probes. No benchmark improvement is established by this paper summary.
pseudocode: For each category: construct padded/truncated histories from the supplied training split; embed items and positions; apply causal attention blocks; score shifted positive items and sampled negatives; minimize binary cross-entropy over nonpadding positions. At inference, score candidates using the last sequence representation. Preserve category routing and select using the supplied macro validation HR@10 protocol.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential attention-based approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Using SASRec unchanged adds little novelty because it is already the required baseline; the supplied idea specifies no new cold-start mechanism.

future_potential.positive: Permitted metadata and history-length diagnostics could motivate extensions for sparse interactions, evaluated within the fixed validation protocol.
future_potential.negative: Such extensions remain hypotheses; paper results do not establish gains on this matched four-category benchmark.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing baseline and diagnostic compatibility contract reduce implementation work.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require consistent training, checkpoint loading, predictor generation and diagnosis adaptation.
